subject: docs/coop/artifacts/gate-harness-naming.v2.json
reviewType: independent, refute not confirm; successor to REJECTED v1

selfCorrection.summary: Both blockers that rejected v1 were mine to catch. I returned ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES on v1 and raised neither. They share one shape, and it is a shape I had not previously recorded.

GHN_V1_B1.whatV1Did: v1 marked DR-G17 sliceStanding REQUIRED-CONDITIONAL and carried a rides field: 'If DR-006 closes by scoped disposition rather than binding recipes, SARIF drops from the preview by that disposition's terms. This identifier then becomes inapplicable, not waived.' It counted G17 inside requiredNow=19.
GHN_V1_B1.whyThatIsWrong: The antecedent had already fired. D-077 owner-recorded route-b.DR-006.preview-disposition.v2 for DR-006, and its adopted text reads 'SARIF drops; cache keys, Coverage, and PlanId stay conceptual.' So at the time v1 was written G17 was inapplicable, not conditional, and counting it inflated the required set.
GHN_V1_B1.whyMyMissIsWorse: I reviewed D-077 myself and consented to it. My D-077 verdict quotes its clause 3 — 'Named D-002 rides remain: SARIF for analyze drops' — as one of the things I verified. Reviewing v1 a short time later, I read the conditional framing, noted the ride was honestly disclosed, and called it consistent, without asking whether the condition had already resolved by an act I had personally passed.

GHN_V1_B2.whatV1Did: v1 counted DR-G03 and DR-G04 inside requiredNow=19 as NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, while declining to supply the exact machine identifiers, OS versions, cache-state protocol, product sign-off and native-Intel procurability verification.
GHN_V1_B2.whyThatIsWrong: D-006 makes the G03/G04 harness-naming act itself the act that pins those things. A naming act that omits them is incomplete by D-006's own terms, so naming those two identifiers produces no real condition-4 naming progress — yet they were counted as though it did.
GHN_V1_B2.whyMyMissIsWorse: I verified the declination and praised it, writing that the artifact 'is refusing a job D-006 assigns to this very act rather than one it was never asked to do.' Having established that the naming act was incomplete on D-006's terms, I did not take the one further step of asking whether an incomplete naming act may count its own gates as named. The inconsistency was entirely inside the document.

selfCorrection.theCommonShape: In both cases the artifact disclosed a dependency and counted the dependent item, and I checked each disclosure in isolation without reconciling it against the count. Neither required information I lacked: B2 was visible within the document, and B1 turned on a decision I had reviewed. My earlier recorded misses were about text I had not read, referents I had not checked, values gone stale, an unread grant field, and an undisplaced authority. This one is different — I read everything and drew no consequence from it.
selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: When an artifact both discloses a dependency and counts the item that depends on it, test whether the disclosure defeats the count. An honestly named blocker still has arithmetic consequences; disclosure is not neutralisation. Concretely: for every conditional standing, ask whether the antecedent has already fired, and check the adopted register rather than the artifact's tense; and for every item counted as done, ask whether the artifact elsewhere admits the work defining 'done' is unmet.

summary: Subject and prompt held, and v1 is unedited. Both blockers are repaired structurally rather than by relabelling. G17 is moved out of the required set into droppedInapplicable with standing INAPPLICABLE-DROPPED-BY-D077 and namingStanding HISTORICAL-IDENTIFIER-RETAINED-NOT-COUNTED. G03 and G04 are moved into reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePins with standing IDENTIFIER-RESERVED-ZERO-C4-PROGRESS, and all three carry an explicit contributeToCondition4NamedCount false. The arithmetic now reconciles two ways: the five-part partition sums to 22 with no overlaps and equals the gate set exactly, and the countable sixteen is precisely D-002's nineteen minus those three. Both parts of my own v1 advisory are also repaired — all four cited digests match live bytes, and the DR-G16 owner cell now carries its provenance parenthetical verbatim.

The arithmetic reconciles two independent ways. First, the five-part partition — countable 16, reserved 2, dropped 1, hygiene 2, blocked 1 — sums to 22, has no overlapping members, and its union equals the 22-gate set exactly. Second, the countable sixteen is precisely D-002's required nineteen with G03, G04 and G17 removed: I expanded D-002's list independently and the resulting set matches requiredNowCountable element for element.

The countCheck's own wording is more careful than v1's. Where v1 said 'Matches file 08's 22-gate table', v2 says 'Countable naming progress if later recorded = 16, not 19. Matches file 08's 22-gate table as a partition, not as a required-now count.' That distinction is the substance of both blockers stated in one sentence.

condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded is corrected and strengthened. It now reads 'from 0 named toward 16 of 16 countable required names', states 'G03/G04 contribute zero until a D-006-conforming successor', 'G17 is dropped (D-077) and must not be counted', and — new in v2 — gives the substantive reason condition 4 still could not be MET even at sixteen of sixteen: 'Condition 4 would still not be MET: G03/G04 machine pins remain.' v1 rested that only on file 08's snapshot not yet matching.

All four cited artifact digests now match live bytes — COORD, file 08, the frozen v1, and route-b.DR-006.preview-disposition.v2 — and two commit pins were added, of which D-077's d401ecd8 resolves to 'D-077: owner-record DR-006 preview Route B disposition' and D-056's 75c981dd to 'D-056: SATISFIED-vs-qualification successor amendment'. acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. The repair is structural: G17 and the G03/G04 pair are not relabelled but moved into named partition classes, given standings that say what they are, and flagged with a boolean that makes the count machine-checkable. I verified the arithmetic two independent ways and both give sixteen. My own advisory is fully discharged, including the DR-G16 parenthetical. I have recorded a self-correction in full, because both blockers were mine to raise and neither needed information I lacked — one turned on a decision I had reviewed and consented to weeks of cycles earlier in this same sequence, and the other was an inconsistency wholly inside the document I was reading. The lesson I am taking is that a disclosed dependency still has arithmetic consequences, and that I should test disclosures against counts rather than crediting them in isolation.
